paths.title: Prepare an agent workflow
paths.audience: Business owners and team leads trying one useful AI task
paths.goal: Leave with one scoped task brief and a clear way to check its first saved result.
prerequisites: Bring one small task and approved sample inputs.
Use the app and account you already have; confirm needed access separately.
paths.boundary: Practice with public or fictional inputs. This path does not install tools, grant access, publish work or start a schedule.

exercise.prompt: Choose a small draft you can check. Write its allowed input, expected output, pass checks and stop rule. Try it only with inputs you may use; save and reopen the result.
exercise.deliverable: A task brief plus a checked saved draft, or an exact missing-capability note.
checks: The brief names the result, source, audience and allowed actions.
Each important claim can be checked against the supplied input.
The saved output reopens; failures and unknowns stay visible.
A next owner and handoff are named. No automatic installation or schedule is claimed.

paths.title: Run the Content Factory
paths.audience: Creators, editors and agency teams turning real source material into useful content
paths.goal: Turn one permitted source into an audience-specific opening and a checked editorial handoff.
prerequisites: Bring one permitted transcript or short source, a title and a draft.
Know who may approve and publish it; this session stops at the draft.
paths.boundary: Produce → Process → Post → Promote remains the maintained method. This practice covers the brief, draft opening and handoff—not a completed publishing or promotion run.

exercise.prompt: Use one allowed source to write a brief and two or three opening sentences. Have a partner trace each factual claim to that source and identify who the piece helps.
exercise.deliverable: A source-linked brief, draft opening, visual plan and editor handoff.
checks: The goal, source content and intended reader agree.
The opening says what the reader can do and why it matters.
Claims and the proposed visual have sources and use permission.
Draft, approved and published states remain separate.

paths.title: Review ads before changing spend
paths.audience: Ad operators and agency owners reviewing a small campaign
paths.goal: Make one evidence-backed keep, stop, change or hold recommendation without changing an account.
prerequisites: Bring a permitted dated export or use a clearly fictional example.
Include the goal, result definition, currency and reporting window.
paths.boundary: Read and recommend only. No campaign launch, account connection, budget change or spending authority is granted by this training.

exercise.prompt: Compare two test rows against the goal set before the test. Recalculate each cost per result. Mark missing inputs as unknown and write one bounded next recommendation.
exercise.deliverable: A reproducible comparison and a Metrics → Analysis → Action note.
checks: Costs and results use matching periods, definitions and units.
Zero or missing denominators do not become a zero cost.
Observed results and possible explanations are separate.
The recommendation names an owner and the approval needed before spend changes.

paths.title: Run clear team operations
paths.audience: Managers and operators handing work between people or agents
paths.goal: Give a teammate a task they can understand, check and hand back without guesswork.
prerequisites: Bring one repeat task and a safe example of its output.
Choose an actual receiving role; confirm acceptance outside this practice.
paths.boundary: Draft the assignment and status update. Sending, new commitments and changing responsibilities follow the team's existing authority.

exercise.prompt: Write an assignment with inputs, allowed actions, output, early review and pass checks. Ask a partner to find one ambiguity. Revise it, then draft a truthful status update.
exercise.deliverable: A revised assignment, review note and unsent status draft.
checks: A fresh reader can identify the starting input and useful output.
The check judges the result, not just whether steps were attempted.
The status distinguishes drafted, delivered and accepted.
The next owner is explicit; acknowledgment is not assumed.

paths.title: Run a digital marketing agency
paths.audience: Agency owners choosing the next improvement across marketing, delivery and money
paths.goal: Map the agency's strongest supported constraint and choose one bounded improvement.
prerequisites: Bring permitted summaries for demand, delivery quality and money, or a fictional case.
Keep client identities, contracts and private financial records out of public sessions.
paths.boundary: This is an agency decision workshop, not a complete paid agency course or advice to change pricing, staffing or contracts. Keep protected courses at their existing source.

exercise.prompt: Map one measure for Marketing, Operations and Finance. State its source and time window, or mark the gap. Choose the best-supported constraint and propose one small action.
exercise.deliverable: A three-function map with one sourced constraint, next owner and check.
checks: Marketing, Operations and Finance are all considered without inventing numbers.
Reported revenue, collected cash, costs and profit are not substituted.
The constraint is supported or explicitly a hypothesis.
The action has an owner, a limit and an observable result to review.

practiceSessions.title: A checked campaign bundle from fictional inputs
practiceSessions.audience: Agency and content operators using the original Tampa fictional exercise
practiceSessions.goal: Save and check a seven-file campaign draft bundle without sending, publishing or spending.

steps.title: 1. Prepare the workspace
steps.instruction: Open the original Tampa task card below. Save it locally. Use your existing assistant and an editor or file workspace. Use only its fictional S1–S4 inputs. No account setup or paid course access is required.

steps.title: 2. Learn the task and its boundaries
steps.instruction: Read the assignment, S1–S4, seven required filenames and copyable prompt in full. Explain the audience, one offer and next action. Name the unsupported proposed claim in S4 and why the pilot notes cannot prove customer results. This is the Process stage; Post and Promote remain proposals.

steps.title: 3. Make and preserve the first attempt
steps.instruction: Give your assistant the complete task card, including the prompt. Save the unedited response as 00-first-response.txt before requesting corrections. Produce the six other named files. If file tools are unavailable, copy each named section into your editor and save it yourself; record that assistance.

steps.title: 4. Check all seven outputs
steps.instruction: Open every saved file. Compare claims with S1–S4, count each draft's words, inspect the one proposed test and job card, and check the booking placeholder and no-live-action boundary. Record failures as well as passes. Use the checks below and the full source instructions.

steps.title: 5. Revise without erasing the evidence
steps.instruction: Keep the first attempt unchanged. Save any corrected files in a separate revised folder and note what changed. Ask another reviewer to check the work when available; label self-check and independent review separately. A passing self-check alone does not establish teaching success.

steps.title: 6. Save, reopen and hand off
steps.instruction: Keep the seven files as the actual deliverables. In the practice record below, retain the first response, checks, revision or no-correction note, and one next owner/action. Download the record, clear or leave this page, then reopen it and the output files. Explain one rejected claim and one remaining permission gate to your reviewer. Downloaded records stay on your device and may contain your text; use fictional or approved public inputs only.

practiceSessions.deliverable: Seven files from the task card plus a locally downloaded/reopened practice record. Keep the first response and any revisions separate. A saved record documents a rehearsal; it does not certify a learner or prove a campaign ran.
checks: All seven exact source filenames are saved and reopened; original first response is preserved.
GCT names one audience, the single fictional offer and the correct next action; all factual claims cite S1–S4.
Claim ledger distinguishes supported, qualified and omitted claims; the doubled-lead guarantee is rejected and pilot limitations remain explicit.
VSL 60–90 words, email 100–150 words, JV introduction 70–110 words; each has a different purpose and the required booking-link placeholder.
Exactly one proposed test has a primary outcome, denominator, proposed threshold, owner, permission gates, measurement caveats and stop condition.
Agent job lists trigger, allowed inputs, all seven outputs, acceptance checks, reviewer/owner, exceptions, private/shared boundary and source version.
Receipt reports only observed actions; no live sending, publishing, spend, connection, installation, schedule, revenue or learner mastery is invented.
Reopened practice record preserves first attempt, check notes, revision and next action; changed-source warnings are reviewed.
